data.why: The page is fully self-contained: it has a built-in kinematic diffraction simulator, a 'Simulate' tab that generates diffraction/real-space images for chosen materials and twist angles, and two ready-made 'Examples' buttons (STM-like graphene 8°, diffraction MoS2 16°) that feed straight into the 'Measure' tab, so no external files are needed.

goals: simulate the diffraction pattern and real-space moire pattern for a chosen twist angle and material pair
measure the twist angle and its uncertainty from a simulated or uploaded diffraction pattern
measure the twist angle from a real-space microscope image (STM, AFM or TEM) via its Fourier transform
check how noise, strain, or off-centre shift affect the measured twist angle and its uncertainty
identify the likely 2D material from an image when the scale (nm or 1/nm per pixel) is known

review.summary: This tree follows TwistScope's simulate-then-measure split. Every screen I opened matches its node's numbers, and it honestly records the parts it could not reach (uploads, moiré-only measurement, the command-line robustness tests). Before filing, it needs the check run's 1° 'Clean' wrong-answer case added, the 028 material mismatch blamed on the wrong width the agent typed rather than the tool, and the Material dropdown and f6 candidate-list descriptions corrected.
